editorial.headline: The Broad Machinery Workshop Behind Indonesia’s Industrial Back Room
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 28199 covers a wide field of general-purpose machinery, nationally open to full foreign ownership but requiring careful Bali scope checking.
editorial.body:
KBLI 28199 is the broad workshop category for general-purpose machinery that does not sit neatly elsewhere. Its Indonesian scope points to the manufacture of practical industrial equipment: fire sprinklers, machines that filter or clean liquids and gases, distillation units, heat exchangers, gas generators, centrifuges, spraying and sandblasting equipment, steam-cleaning machines, vending machines, attic ventilation fans, tape measures and similar hand tools, non-optical machinist precision tools, and non-electric brazing or soldering equipment. It also includes the manufacture of components and equipment for that machinery.

The common thread is not a single product but a manufacturing role: machinery that helps factories, buildings, workshops, refineries, chemical plants, beverage operations, and other industrial settings move, clean, press, distil, ventilate, dispense, measure, or apply materials. The record is deliberately wide. It reaches from fire extinguishers and spray guns to calendering presses, winding machines and their cylinders, and rectification machinery for oil refineries and chemical or beverage industries. A company registering this activity is therefore not describing ordinary trading or installation work; it is identifying itself as a maker of machinery and related equipment within this broad general-purpose field.

On scale, the record is unusually open. Micro, small, medium, and large businesses are all listed as eligible scales. Nationally, the foreign-investment picture is also clear: the activity is marked TERBUKA, with a pma_max_asing value of 100, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national record treats the activity as open to foreign ownership up to 100%. There is no separate lower ceiling in the slim record, and there is no basis here to add one.

Bali is the more careful reading. The record does not mark this activity as simply blocked: l4_bali_blocked is false. But its Bali status is Blocked (scope-dependent), and the reason is explicit: "OSS risk at scale Besar is low on SOME scope(s) but higher on other(s): registrable as PMA in Bali only by declaring the higher-risk scope (e.g. PPMSE for platform-trade codes) — verify live OSS per exact activity". That warning sits beside the moratorium rule that Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, island-wide and permanent. So the honest conclusion is precise rather than dramatic: nationally, KBLI 28199 is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, PMA registration depends on the exact declared activity and its live OSS risk treatment, because some scopes may fall into the Bali moratorium logic while others may be registrable only through the higher-risk declaration path described in the record.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, KBLI 28199 is foreign-open up to 100%; in Bali, the decisive issue is the exact activity declared in OSS.
